full_judgment: 22. In the case of People's Republic of Bangladesh Vs. Abdul Hoque, 1982 BLD (AD) 143 it was held that "the respondent was born in the territory now comprised in Bangladesh but his temporary absence is covered by the proviso quoted above and the law says "he shall be deemed to continue to be resident in Bangladesh, notwithstanding his temporary residence in a country which was at war or engaged in military operations against Bangladesh." In the said case one Abdul Haque was directed to leave the country by an order dated 9.3.78 and this order was challenged in a writ petition before the High Court Division on which a Rule was issued and ultimately the said Rule was made absolute. Against the said order, the Government preferred the appeal before the Appellate Division. The case of the detenu Abdul Haque was that he was born in Satkhira within the territory of Bangladesh and in November, 1971 he had gone to Pakistan and in 1975 he came back to Bangladesh with a Pakistani passport. He surrendered his passport to the Government and applied for citizenship of Bangladesh. The Government, however, refused to grant him citizenship and asked him to leave the country by issuing order under the Foreigners Act, 1946 in which the aforesaid observations were-made.
